title: My Chemical Romance Top the Charts, 20 Years On
summary:
Twenty years after it first came out, My Chemical Romance's album "The Black Parade" is Number One again. The new 20th anniversary version topped the Billboard 200 chart. It is the band's first Number One album in almost 25 years.

The new version sold 78,000 equivalent album units across more than 20 formats and versions, Billboard reports. The first album came out in 2006. It was the band's third album, a rock opera in the style of Queen, with the Top Ten hit "Welcome to the Black Parade." It first reached Number Two.

The band put out the 20th anniversary version on October 23. Sales of physical copies pushed it to the top. On Friday, the band also got its first Number One on the United Kingdom's album chart.

The old album beat a new album by Olivia Rodrigo. Midweek guesses said My Chemical Romance would win by a thousand sales. Rodrigo cheered them on and posted a clip from their show at Citi Field in New York, which she went to earlier this year.

The band is now on its Long Live the Black Parade tour, which started in 2025. Last year, they played two sold-out nights at Wembley Stadium in London.
why_it_matters: Music you love can stay popular for years, and old songs can become new favorites.
